findings.topic: Jordan requires an NFL roster-status gate
findings.text: Houston's current official roster lists Jawhar Jordan under Practice Squad. Its transaction table records his August 31 practice-squad signing. The player profile displays 2025 totals of 43 carries for 193 yards and seven catches for 34 yards. Those are historical season totals, not Week 5 2026 production. No Week 6 elevation or current usage was established here.
findings.confidence: HIGH for displayed official records; game-day role unresolved

findings.topic: Historical praise is not a current depth-chart promotion
findings.text: The July KPRC interview describes improved third-down execution and a roster competition. Treat it as dated scouting context, not evidence of an October promotion or receiving workload.
findings.confidence: HIGH on source date; LOW for extrapolation to Week 6

findings.text: Seattle did not practice Tuesday; Denver held a walkthrough. Both reports use estimated participation. JSN remained limited/ankle; Charbonnet limited/knee; Holani full/ribs-knee. Denver listed Surtain and Hufanga as estimated nonparticipants and Moss limited. Denver says game statuses come Wednesday. These are not final Thursday clearance or observed full-speed workload.
findings.confidence: HIGH for official reports; future availability unresolved

findings.topic: Trade theses are conditional, price-dependent forecasts
findings.text: Moorman compares his half-PPR rest-of-season views against ECR, favoring opportunity over recent points and distinguishing buys, sells and holds. His Hall discussion anticipates possible Allen competition after a return; Mitchell is discussed as receiving-depth with contingent upside. Those are testable opinions, not confirmed future workload. Quoted usage estimates and all injury forecasts in that article were not independently validated here.
findings.confidence: B for transparent accessible reasoning; C for uncrosschecked usage and forecast claims

findings.topic: Chart numbers are not trade-clearing prices
findings.text: FantasyPros describes its chart as analyst-ranking-derived and explicitly league-dependent. A positional rank match or equal summed chart value does not establish equal team utility, especially in a two-for-one trade.
findings.confidence: HIGH for stated method; no calibrated trade-price accuracy established

educational_lesson.central_method: Evaluate a proposed trade as a change in the feasible lineup portfolio across future role and injury scenarios, rather than adding positional ranks or last-week points.
educational_lesson.mathematics: For each future week and scenario, evaluate the best eligible lineup using only information that would be available by lineup lock. Expected trade benefit is the scenario-weighted difference in lineup points after versus before, including any player displaced to make roster room. Apply any playoff-week or risk weights explicitly. Do not combine fantasy points and dollars without a declared common utility conversion.
educational_lesson.synthetic_example: Two starting slots, deterministic example only: before a trade, A projects 18 and replacement R projects 8, totaling 26. Receiving B=14 and C=13 produces 27, a gain of 1, although comparing B+C=27 against A alone=18 misleadingly suggests a gain of 9. If both received players compete for one usable slot, the result changes again. These are invented teaching inputs, not player projections.
challenged_assumptions: Equal positional rank does not imply equal surplus value across positions.
Regression toward a baseline is not a promise of imminent touchdowns.
A famous player's low price is not a bargain unless expected usable production exceeds what is surrendered.
A practice-squad player does not receive a positive opportunity projection merely because a historical highlight looks strong.
educational_lesson.test: Freeze role-state probabilities, expected routes/carries/goal-line usage, injury duration assumptions, feasible replacements and the offered price before the trade decision. Compare the scenario model against chart-sum and recent-score baselines on later chronological weeks. Record proposed, accepted and rejected trades separately; only confirmed actions enter realized team results. Measure lineup-point forecast error and opportunity-share error; evaluate intervals and calibration only when numerical probabilities and sufficient resolved cases exist.
educational_lesson.failure_conditions: Reject the added complexity if held-out lineup forecasts do not improve or any apparent advantage disappears after including rejected candidates, unavailable replacements and displaced-player costs. Preserve failed cases and original estimates.
educational_lesson.evidence_grade: Mathematical accounting is exact under stated assumptions. Probabilities, projections and incremental predictive benefit remain unvalidated.

research_proposals.name: Role uncertainty drives misvaluation after injury-replacement weeks
research_proposals.mechanism: Managers may price a replacement's latest points as permanent workload or overdiscount the returning starter.
research_proposals.test: Predefine return-date scenarios and post-return carry, route and goal-line shares; compare to next four games and a static recent-volume baseline.
research_proposals.failure_condition: No held-out gain, or improvements are attributable to hindsight injury updates.

research_proposals.name: Roster-status gating reduces wasted speculative evaluations
research_proposals.mechanism: Historical player profiles can appear current while omitting active/practice-squad status.
research_proposals.test: Track candidates excluded pending an elevation and those later activated, with opportunity outcomes and opportunity costs; retain false negatives.
research_proposals.failure_condition: Gate discards useful early contingent stashes without offsetting decision benefit.
